deferredGates.exitCriteria: 1.9 completion gate: resolve provisional L3 tool, movement and trap semantics against original-engine evidence. Complete environmental effects, original movie audio and story transitions. Extend L2 original-engine comparisons. Record every L2/L3 winning route and verify continuous campaign progression, L2 survivor carry-over, at least 50 survivors at the end of each L3 tribe, endings, saved-run recovery, replay identity and result records.
deferredGates.progress: 6 October: the source-matched, headless and muted strict L3 gate passes a 306-entry fixture manifest, 74 of 90 standalone wins, 155 double-replayed carried fixtures and 68 linked campaign results. Original DOS frame evidence corrected Egyptian 27 connected source-stair motion. The source-matched runtime suite and full completion gate pass after the correction, but Egyptian 27 has no winning fixture and original DOS tool, Buzzard and route timing parity remain open. On 8 October, exact Shadow 21 no-input DOS evidence showed its placed prisoner alive and its Buzzard stationary for 2,734 captured frames. The runtime now treats that byte-identified Shadow 21 scene as an inert Buzzard hatch run, with a focused regression. This closes only the observed no-input discrepancy; general Buzzard activation and combat parity remain open. Classic 23 now saves 12, loses one and retains 26 in reserve at carried population 36. Its population-20 standalone route has the same saved and lost counts. Classic 24 saves ten, loses none and retains 28 in reserve at population 38. Classic 25 now saves all 12 released and placed actors, loses none and retains 28 in reserve at population 38; its population-20 standalone route also saves all 12. Classic enters level 26 with population 40. The first linked gaps are Classic 26/population 40, Shadow 121/population one and Egyptian 224/population one. Sixteen standalone wins remain missing. Classic levels 26–30 each contain two placed extras, so a final count of at least 50 now requires zero further losses. Stronger strict standalone routes now retain 18 of 20 in Shadow 110 and all 20 in Shadow 111, Shadow 112, Shadow 113, Shadow 114 and Egyptian 214; these do not close their continuous-campaign or original DOS parity gates. Egyptian 218/population four saves three; existing 219/population three saves three, 220/population three saves two, and new 221/population two saves both incoming lemmings. The new Egyptian 221 standalone fixture saves two but loses 19. Carried Egyptian 222/population two and 223/population one each save one and lose two, leaving one for level 224; survivor retention remains open. A Classic 29 standalone fallback saves one of 20 and does not resolve carried survivor retention. A fixture audit found repeated actions on one lemming in one tick in 16 of 74 standalone and 30 of 155 carried routes; neither new Classic 25 fixture nor the new Shadow 14 fixtures have a repeated actor-tick; original DOS input timing remains unverified. Shadow 108 retains all ten released actors at population 22. Shadow 109 saves 11 and loses one at population 22. The new Shadow 110 carried route saves 11, loses three and retains ten in reserve at population 23. The new Shadow 11 route repeats a seven-input pattern for all ten hatch actors. At population 21 it saves ten, loses none and retains 11 in reserve. Shadow 12 now saves all ten released actors, loses none and retains 11 in reserve at population 21; the same route retains all 20 standalone. Shadow 13 now saves all ten released actors, loses none and retains 11 in reserve at population 21; the same route retains all 20 standalone. Shadow 14 at population 21 now saves all ten released actors, loses the placed extra and retains 11 in reserve, preserving all 21 incoming actors. Shadow 15 at population 21 still saves one, loses 11 and retains 11 in reserve, carrying 12 into level 16. Egyptian 214 now saves ten, loses three placed prisoners and keeps three in reserve at population 13, carrying 13 into level 215. Level 217 still reduces the chain to four and Egyptian 213 loses ten, so no 50-survivor Egyptian campaign is proved. A new offscreen, muted app test passed exact L3 disk checkpoint restoration, input replay, rejection of changed source or state, and 40-tick continuation using current source and existing development bundle resources. Original DOS release cadence, further tool and trap parity, three complete 30-level campaigns with at least 50 survivors, media, recovery from the actual 1.8 release-candidate package, physical input and release packaging remain open. The latest separate L2 checkpoint still lacks 45 wins. Egyptian 25 source object 5009 now decodes as a four-grenade box and 5007 as a clock. The source-matched runtime suite passes its 66-box regression. Twelve standalone and 23 carried fixtures with those source objects were reconstructed from preserved inputs, then double-replayed. The rebuilt manifest, full standalone gate and carried chain verify 74 standalone fixtures, 155 carried fixtures and 68 linked results. Egyptian 29 now has a two-Spade native standalone fixture that saves two, loses ten and retains ten in reserve; original-DOS timing remains unverified. Classic 28's seven guide-aligned actions execute through its first upward Sucker state. Shadow 121 has exploratory native Brick and Spade checkpoints. Its recorded up-right Spade input reaches empty native terrain, while the adjacent up-left branch cuts 16 source-decoded terrain pixels; its distinct source-matched continuation still has no candidate. The guide's vertical final-car stack and original-DOS action timing are unverified. Egyptian 27 source capture now verifies the guide opening as visual-targeted Walker reversal followed immediately by the third-control Jumper arc. Its Buzzard remains static for 18 seconds after those inputs. Its source tick conversion, later guide inputs, Buzzard activation and complete-route timing remain unverified. The exact Shadow 22 no-input DOS hatch references now keep the placement-33 Buzzard out of the lower-left hatch corridor; the scoped runtime regression and strict 306-hash fixture verifier pass, but a current 40-second source-matched search saves no Lemming. Its wider Psycho Buzzard activation, movement and combat parity remain unverified. The native L3 canvas now has the original documented right-click carrier control: direct carrier selection, mid-air carrier cycling, a red carrier marker and same-group targeting priority. Its focused headless, muted targeting test passes. This does not verify original UI artwork or physical input. Both games remain Preview. See 1.8SequelVerification.md for exact source, fixture and replay hashes and remaining limits.

deferredGates.exitCriteria: 1.7 gate: run every advertised level with no unsupported mechanics. Compare real reference replays, rescue frames, final state, destructive masks, gadget effects, animation states and recovery against the pinned CE oracle. Verify pack progress, changed-content rejection and lawful distribution inputs in the native app.
deferredGates.progress: 28 September: the NeoLemmix 12.14 and CE 1.2.0 compatibility gate is closed. The strict pinned corpus passes 794 levels and 250,996 deterministic ticks with 42 benign content diagnostics, zero unsupported levels, and zero import or render failures. All 21 current skills pass focused tests. The March 2025 Redux corpus completes all 160 native and recovered runs; all 158 exact-version routes retain stable pack, level, source-revision and progress identity, while two version mismatches remain classified separately. An independent live-memory export from the pinned CE executable matches all 160 native terminal states, including scalar, lemming, gadget, inventory and live-terrain fields. The live CE visual matrix covers all 21 skills, 68 selected frames, seven style families, live terrain, triggered and secondary gadget animation, athlete recoloring, overlap ordering and NO_OVERWRITE; every frame has zero mutually visible RGB differences. Native recovery and pack integration pass, changed content is rejected, and bundled inputs are limited to the owner-approved CE levels and 26 DMA styles; community styles remain player-supplied. See 1.7Roadmap.md, NeoLemmixFinalStateOracle.md, NeoLemmixReplayCaptureOracle.md and ReleaseReadiness/1.7NeoLemmixPreparation.md.

deferredGates.exitCriteria: Verify app and controller interruption on real hardware. Add versioned in-progress checkpoints and crash recovery before mobile suspend/termination support. Verify save migrations and rollback with real prior releases.
deferredGates.progress: 15 September: all existing checkpoint, corruption, stale-writer and recovery tests pass. Ten new trials kill an isolated writer process during checkpoint updates, then validate the recovered checkpoint with a fresh reader. These pass. Classic wins now preserve validated input routes separately from recovery checkpoints. Physical interruption, installed prior-release migration and power-loss coverage remain distinct from these process tests. See CampaignClosure-2026-09-22.md.

deferredGates.exitCriteria: Test the complete first-launch-to-results flow with physical Xbox, PlayStation and Switch-layout controllers. Add remapping and device glyphs, touch targeting, readable UI scaling, reduced motion/flash controls and VoiceOver navigation without forcing OG gameplay.
deferredGates.progress: Earlier beta testing passed complete software-driven journeys on Apple silicon and Intel/Rosetta. F retains the reached speed after release; mouse and keyboard speed arrows apply immediately from 1x. Green handover initials and the previous-level retry button were rendered and tested with real mouse events. Existing keyboard/controller routing, targeting, fonts, scalable menus, hints and interruption tests passed. Physical controllers and full VoiceOver remain unverified.

deferredGates.exitCriteria: Measure complete frame times, memory growth and audio under sustained 10x play, nukes, replays and repeated engine switches. Test physical Intel, minimum supported macOS, SDR/HDR, multiple displays and high refresh rates.
deferredGates.progress: 15 September: a repeated 20-scenario run exposed utility-priority replay encoder stalls under concurrent heavy work. User-initiated encoder priority completed all 20 scenarios with all 8,013 movie frames and no GPU errors. Queue size and the 500 ms input-blocking bound remain unchanged. Resident memory did not grow across five passes. Observed fast-forward was only 1.14–1.45× under contention, so sustained 10×, audible audio and the physical hardware matrix remain open. See PerformanceMeasurementClosure.md.

deferredGates.exitCriteria: 2.0 release gate: build and test the shared library with the iOS SDK. Implement a UIKit/Metal app shell, precise touch selection, safe-area layouts, audio/session interruptions, checkpoints, thermal budgets and device tests. A Package.swift deployment declaration is not an iOS app.
deferredGates.progress: 25 September: the repository now has a version 1.3 UIKit application target for iPhone and iPad, shared mobile-core and UI modules, nearest-neighbour Metal output, direct targeting, pan and anchored zoom, safe-area controls, explicit-resume audio and application lifecycle handling, atomic versioned checkpoints, thermal budgets, privacy metadata, an app icon and an iPhone/iPad CI matrix. All 42 package tests pass, including 13 focused mobile tests for staged import safety, stale-writer rejection, a Classic jumping regression and exact Classic, L2 and L3 checkpoint restoration. Xcode 26.6 compiled Debug and optimised Release Swift builds for both Simulator architectures and an unsigned optimised arm64 device build with the iOS 26.5 SDK. GitHub Actions run 36027222792 passed the source gate for commit 929cc3b6ed69e620471acc1180c7bcf44008d957 with Xcode 16.4, then passed two UI tests with no failures on iPhone 16 Pro and iPad Pro 11-inch (M4) Simulators running iOS 18.5. The Simulator launch-and-rotation gate is closed for that commit. Physical touch, interruption, audio, thermal, VoiceOver, signing, TestFlight and App Store evidence remain open. The player-facing mobile slice imports Classic DOS data only; L2 and L3 mobile import and renderers are not claimed. See 2.0Roadmap.md and 1.3MobileHandoff.md.
